notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($831,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Ohio county candidates file campaign finance reports with their county board of elections, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023, as the village reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Ashtabula County and, unless the municipality has left it, the surrounding township.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($67,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: Ohio local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county board of elections, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
